Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TNF, wounding, or growth factor), then track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and chromatin accessibility at defined times after washout, including weeks later. Persistence of AP-1-dependent open regions after the stimulus and AP-1 levels have returned to baseline would indicate a memory-like state.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation to test maintenance versus initiation
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) FOS, JUN, or the BATF family to remove AP-1 either during priming or after memory is established. Then measure accessibility and the secondary-stimulus transcriptional response. If depletion during priming blocks memory but depletion afterward does not, AP-1 is needed only for initiation. Loss of memory after later depletion would show it is also needed for maintenance.

ideas.title: Secondary-challenge response assays (primed versus naive)
ideas.description: Compare the RNA-seq and nascent transcription (PRO-seq) response of primed and naive cells to a second stimulus, and relate the strength of the enhanced response to AP-1 motif content at the affected genes. Include dose and time-gap titrations to define how long the memory lasts and whether it is AP-1-dependent.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing across divisions
ideas.description: Do paired scRNA/scATAC-seq together with a heritable barcode or clonal tracking in primed cells across several divisions. This tests whether AP-1-associated accessibility states are inherited by daughter cells and whether clonal sister cells share the memory more than random cells do.

ideas.title: Targeted epigenome editing and AP-1 site perturbation
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate or block specific AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, and use dCas9-based tools to force AP-1 recruitment or histone-mark changes at them without a stimulus. Then check whether accessibility, H3K27ac, and enhanced re-induction are lost or created. This tests whether AP-1 binding at those sites is sufficient and necessary for memory, and whether it works through cooperating factors or chromatin remodelers such as BAF.
